missionText: Our mission is to inspire, inform, educate, and entertain humanity — all from the comfort of your very own stall.
humorBody:
A tourist lands in Las Vegas and checks into his hotel.

At the front desk he asks, "What's the secret to winning big in this town?"

The clerk smiles and says, "Simple. Just remember that the house always wins."

The tourist laughs. "Not me. I'm different."

He heads straight to the casino.

By midnight he's lost $500.

By 2:00 AM he's lost $1,500.

By 4:00 AM he's lost the rest of his gambling money.

Determined to turn things around, he goes back to his room, takes a shower, puts on his lucky shirt, and returns to the casino.

A cocktail waitress sees him walking back in and asks, "Feeling lucky?"

The tourist says, "No."

"Then why are you back?"

The tourist shrugs and says,

"Because according to my bank account, I apparently work here now."
mainFeatureBody:
The product you are seeing today was first conceived more than a decade ago. At the time, it existed only as an idea on a piece of paper, a criminal record that seemed impossible to overcome, and a belief that even the most difficult seasons of life can produce something meaningful.

What followed was a journey through more than 300 cities, countless lessons, and a deeper understanding of what truly matters. Along the way, one truth revealed itself again and again:

The pursuit of love and righteousness leads to life, prosperity, and honor.

Potty Favor was born from that belief—a simple idea with a simple mission: to inspire, inform, educate, and entertain people in the one place everyone eventually visits.
secondaryFeatureTitle: WHY LAS VEGAS IS ONE OF THE MOST FASCINATING CITIES ON EARTH
secondaryFeatureBody:
Most cities were built because of geography.

Some were built near rivers. Others were built near oceans, railroads, factories, farmland, or natural resources.

Las Vegas was different.

A little more than a century ago, the Las Vegas Valley was mostly desert. Summers were brutally hot. Rainfall was scarce. Few people would have looked at the landscape and imagined it becoming one of the most recognizable cities on Earth.

Yet today, millions of visitors arrive every year from every corner of the globe.

What makes Las Vegas remarkable isn't simply the casinos. It's the concentration of human ambition.

Within a few miles, you'll find entrepreneurs launching companies, entertainers chasing dreams, chefs building restaurants, athletes competing at the highest levels, engineers constructing mega-resorts, and visitors celebrating some of the biggest moments of their lives.

People come to Las Vegas for weddings, conventions, vacations, concerts, sporting events, trade shows, business deals, reunions, and once-in-a-lifetime experiences.

In many ways, the city has become a crossroads for humanity.

On any given day, someone from Tokyo might share an elevator with someone from London, Toronto, Nashville, Sydney, or São Paulo. Few places in the world create that kind of daily interaction.

Las Vegas is also home to some of the most impressive feats of construction ever attempted.

The Bellagio fountains, the Sphere, Allegiant Stadium, the Las Vegas Convention Center, and countless resort properties required enormous teams of architects, engineers, designers, tradespeople, and visionaries to bring them to life.

Many visitors see the finished product.

Locals know the real story.

Behind every resort, restaurant, stage show, and attraction are thousands of workers who keep the city running every day.

Electricians. Painters. Plumbers. Housekeepers. Bartenders. Servers. Security officers. Drivers. Technicians. Carpenters. Landscapers.

Las Vegas shines because millions of hours of work happen behind the scenes.

The city also continues to reinvent itself.

What began as a railroad stop became a gambling destination. What became a gambling destination evolved into an entertainment capital. Today, Las Vegas is increasingly known for professional sports, conventions, technology conferences, dining, live entertainment, and entrepreneurship.

The city refuses to stand still.

Perhaps that's why so many people are drawn here.

Las Vegas represents possibility.

Some visitors arrive hoping to win money.

Others arrive hoping to win something more valuable—a new opportunity, a new relationship, a new career, a new idea, or a new beginning.

The desert has a way of reminding people that extraordinary things can emerge from unlikely places.

And maybe that's the real story of Las Vegas.

Not the lights.

Not the casinos.

Not even the entertainment.

The real story is what happens when people believe something remarkable can be built where others see only empty space.

That's a lesson worth remembering—whether you're building a city, a business, or a life.
